(2) σ 0 ≠ p: I⁻(γ̃ s₀, Ũ) is open (Causality.isOpen_Iminus) and contains p, σ is continuous within Ioc 0 1 at 0 (CurveOn.continuousOn), and 𝓝[Ioc 0 1] 0 is NeBot, so some σ t, t ∈ (0, 1], lies in the diamond. b_report: PROVED, not only argued: Causal.Causality.not_pastBoundaryChart_of_flrwTypeB_of_isClosed_le (and its local, globally hyperbolic and time-reversed forms). Let M be T2 and second countable, with ≤_M closed and antisymmetric, and let W be causally arc-connected with (B). Then W has a past boundary chart at no point. There is no (A), no future one-connectedness, no field (iii) and no last conjunct of (vi). The planner's partial argument ('σ extended to the future meets the Cauchy surface of (B) at γ̃ s') is replaced by a two-case split: either σ 1 ∈ J⁺(S, W), so σ meets S by (2.4), or σ 1 ∈ J⁻(S, W), so σ 1 ≤_W z ≪_W γ̃ s with z ∈ S. Both give σ t ≤ γ̃ s for some t, and (3) is symmetric. Only ≤ is needed by the closing step, so push-up is not. Second countability and causal arc-connectedness of W enter only through (2.4) and the split. Whether (B) alone suffices without them is not decided.

findings: No paper label is involved: 2312.07443 is not ledgered. These findings concern the programme's design and Sbierski's argument in ETT.

The planner's reading is a theorem. On a T2 space with ≤_M closed and antisymmetric, (A) alone excludes a past boundary chart (not_pastBoundaryChart_of_flrwTypeA_of_isClosed_le). It needs no (B), no future one-connectedness, no causal arc-connectedness and no second countability.

(B) alone also excludes a chart in such an ambient, on a second countable space with W causally arc-connected (not_pastBoundaryChart_of_flrwTypeB_of_isClosed_le). This decides the optional question. In a closed, antisymmetric ambient, neither (A) nor (B) can be shown needed. A witness separating them, in either direction, needs an ambient whose ≤ is not closed or not antisymmetric on every open U ⊇ W ∪ Ũ, by the local forms. For the (A)-needed direction it may alternatively violate second countability or causal arc-connectedness of W. Item 4 of the journal, and the keeper's proposal of an instance where exactly one of (A), (B) fails, cannot be served by any model whose ≤ is closed and antisymmetric (for the (A)-needed direction: on a second countable space with W causally arc-connected).

Neither theorem uses field (iii) or the last conjunct of (vi). In a closed antisymmetric ambient these fields are idle. They are what Sbierski's proof uses to carry σ 1 into I⁺(S, W) in a possibly non-closed C⁰ ambient. This bears on OQ-159 (are the six fields the notion of record?) and presupposes no answer.

This argument cannot take antisymmetry at W alone, as not_pastBoundaryChart_of_flrwType does. The argument concludes σ t̄ = p with p ∉ W, so antisymmetry must hold for a relation that sees p, here ≤_U with U ⊇ W ∪ Ũ. The same goes for closedness: both limits, (p, σ t) → (p, σ 0) and (σ t_s, γ̃ s) → (σ t̄, p), end at points of Ũ, possibly off W.
(A) and (B) are each used at very few instances. (A) is used for two curves only, γ̃ and σ over (0, 1]. (B) is used at the points σ t and γ̃ s only. The FlrwType theorem used (B) at γ̃ s₀ only.

The planner's step (4), 'a subsequence of the t_s converges', is realised without sequences. The set {(t, s) ∈ [0, 1]² | σ t ≤_U γ̃ s} is closed (isClosed_inter_preimage_setOf_le), hence compact. Its projection to s is closed and contains (0, 1], so it contains 0. No countability of M is used, as the planner expected.
questions: '≤_M closed' is read as IsClosed {z : M × M | C.le ⊤ z.1 z.2}, the library's form (the conclusion of GloballyHyperbolic.isClosed_le). The local forms read '≤_U closed in U × U' as closure {z | C.le U z.1 z.2} ∩ U ×ˢ U ⊆ {z | C.le U z.1 z.2}, the shape of the scaffold's IsCausallyClosedOn U (CausalScaffold.GerochEquiv:108). That shape is written inline here because a strict-bound module cannot import the scaffold. At graduation the two could be folded together.

'(B) alone' is read as '(B) in place of (A), keeping the hypotheses of not_pastBoundaryChart_of_flrwType that (2.4) needs': second countability and causal arc-connectedness of W. Future one-connectedness is dropped. Whether (B) excludes a chart without second countability or without causal arc-connectedness is not decided here.

Comparing two past-inextensible curves through a Cauchy surface S ⊆ I⁻(x, W): either the end point is in J⁺(S, W) and (2.4) makes the curve meet S, or it is in J⁻(S, W) (Causal.Causality.IsCauchySurfaceOn.mem_Jplus_union_Jminus, the split from exists_inextensible_of_t1_secondCountable). Either way the curve has a point ≤_W x, and push-up is not needed when only ≤ is concluded.
